name: Cessna 336/337 Skymaster
variants: O-2A / O-2B (US military forward air control)
summary: Unusual centerline-thrust twin with one tractor and one pusher engine on a twin-boom tail, built 1963–1982; the USAF flew it as the O-2 forward air control aircraft.

wings: High wing braced by a strut on each side
Plain, constant-chord panels with no engines on them
engines: One engine and propeller in the nose
A second pusher engine and prop behind the cabin, between the tail booms
fuselage: Short, pod-style cabin with big side windows
Fixed gear on the 336, retractable on the 337
tail: Twin booms running back from the wing to twin fins and rudders
Horizontal stabilizer spans between the booms behind the rear prop

tellTales: Propellers at both the nose and the rear of the cabin
Twin tail booms joined by a horizontal stabilizer
Strut-braced high wing with no engines on it

confusedWith.howToTell: The 182 has a single engine and a single fin on a normal fuselage; the Skymaster has a rear pusher prop and twin tail booms.
The Islander has both engines on the wing and a conventional single tail with no booms; the Skymaster has its engines on the fuselage centerline.
